title: fullcycle never asks a person before clean removes the build trees: its phases get the phase list on stdin, and since 0088 a nested gate reports no person
body:
## Summary

**A person at a terminal who runs `devbin fullcycle` without `--force` is never asked before the build trees go. clean refuses "no tty" every time.** This predates 0088. Measured under a pty with a person's `y` waiting (`run_tty_answer`), on a rust fixture that has a build command:

| commit                   | `devbin clean rust` alone | `devbin fullcycle`, whose first phase is `clean rust --force-blocked` |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `07b661a^` (before 0088) | asks                      | refuses "no tty"                                                      |
| `84f9870`                | asks                      | refuses "no tty"                                                      |

Found by dc on 2026-09-18 while reviewing 0088 row 2 at `84f9870`. vc asked for it to be filed separately, so it does not block 0088's close. The probe is in dc's scratchpad at `r0088/arm.bats`.

## Two causes, one old and one from 0088

**1. The phase loop hands every phase the phase list as stdin.** `_fullcycle_run` reads `done < <(_fullcycle_phases)` (`lib/cmd/fullcycle`, the loop's last line), so the child devbin for each phase inherits that pipe as stdin. Before 0088, clean asked only when `-t 0` held, which it never does there. The comment above the phase `case` says the opposite ("NO `< /dev/null` ... here it would also defeat `clean`'s confirmation"). It has been false for as long as the loop has read its input this way.

**2. Since 0088 row 2, a gate nested inside another gate always reports no person.** fullcycle is itself gated (`run_gate --label fullcycle ... -- _fullcycle_run`), so every phase runs with stdin at `/dev/null`. The child devbin's gate then sets `DEVBIN_GATE_TTY=0` from its own stdin. That value is always set on purpose, so that a stale `1` in the environment cannot stand (0088 row 2, second amendment, `84f9870`). **So fixing cause 1 alone no longer brings the prompt back.** The child cannot tell a parent gate's `1` from a stale one.

**The consent notice is accurate only because of the defect.** It says "clean asks on the tty, and refuses without one. That is the refusal you will meet." At a terminal, a person meets the refusal too.

## Options

**A. Trust a parent gate's `1` across a devbin child boundary.** run_gate would also export a marker that only a gate sets, such as the run id it ran under. A child gate whose stdin is not a terminal takes the inherited `1` only when that marker matches its own inherited `DEVBIN_RUN_ID`. A stale `DEVBIN_GATE_TTY=1` in a person's shell has no matching marker, so it still reads 0. Cost: run_gate's rule stops being "look at your own stdin". It becomes a two-variable rule with an inheritance path, and every nested gate (fullcycle's phases, `dormancy`'s legs, any project handler calling devbin) can then read a `1` it did not measure. Cause 1 still needs its own fix.

**B. fullcycle asks the question itself, once, at the top, where its gate's flag is true.** It runs `clean --dry-run` (0042) to show what goes, asks on the flag through `/dev/tty`, and on a `y` passes `--force` to the clean phase. 0047's rule is "never `--force` unasked", and here the person has been asked. run_gate is not touched, and the flag's rule stays one site and one variable. Costs:
- The prompt moves from clean to fullcycle, so the question clean asks and the one fullcycle asks must not drift. That argues for one confirm helper, lifted out of `_clean_confirm` into `lib/helpers`.
- ST0007 AC-5.3 (a resumed release prompts before its first push) needs the same helper. That makes three callers and one home.

**C. Declare it.** fullcycle without `--force` refuses at a terminal by design. Rewrite the loop comment and the consent notice to say "pass `--force`", and fix nothing else. Cost: a verb whose contract is "from a total clean" has no interactive path at all. A person has to choose between a refusal and removing without a question.

**In every option, the loop should stop feeding phases on stdin** (`while IFS= read -r phase <&3; ... done 3< <(_fullcycle_phases)`). A phase that reads stdin would otherwise eat the phases after it. Today every child gate starts its tool with `/dev/null`, so nothing does, but that protection belongs to the child and could change without anyone noticing.

## Recommendation

**B, with the confirm lifted into one helper that clean, fullcycle and the release core's AC-5.3 prompt all call, and the loop moved to fd 3.** It keeps 0088's rule where hv put it, one site and one variable. It asks once, at the one place that knows a person is there, and shows what will go before asking. It also gives AC-5.3 its helper instead of a third copy of the pattern. A stays open for a nested caller that genuinely has to ask from inside a child. None exists today.

**Arms, whichever option lands**, each red first:
- At a terminal, `devbin fullcycle` without `--force` asks, and a `y` removes the trees.
- An `n` removes nothing and stops the cycle before the build.
- With stdin piped, it refuses with no question.
- A phase that reads stdin does not eat the phases after it.

## Resolution

**hv ruled option B (vc's decision 19). Built by vc at `b729e10`; reviewed and closed by dc on 2026-09-18, with three arms added from the review.**
- `ask_person` (`lib/helpers`) is the one home for the question. It returns 0 on a y, 1 on any other answer, and 2 when nobody can be asked. `_clean_confirm` and `_fullcycle_confirm` both call it, and ST0007 AC-5.3 will too.
- Without `--force`, fullcycle previews the clean phase's own command plus `--dry-run`, asks once inside its own gate, and on a y runs the cycle with `--force` passed to clean. An n, or nobody to ask, stops at rc 1 with nothing removed.
- The phase loop reads the phase list on fd 3 and closes it for each phase.
- The consent notice and the dry-run preview now say that fullcycle asks.

dc's mutants, each on a fresh copy of `51f4578`, were run against the whole of `fullcycle.bats` plus the tty, 0088 and 0090 arms in `clean.bats` (62 arms). The no-op controls (the file unchanged, and a changed comment) stay green at 62 of 62.

| mutant                                                | result               |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| `ask_person` answers 0 to anything                    | KILLED (2 red)       |
| `ask_person`'s nobody-to-ask 2 folded into 1          | KILLED (2 red)       |
| `ask_person` reads stdin, not /dev/tty                | KILLED (2 red)       |
| fullcycle asks only WITH `--force`                    | KILLED (33 red)      |
| fullcycle asks with `--force` too                     | KILLED (30 red)      |
| fullcycle proceeds when nobody can be asked           | KILLED (1 red)       |
| the preview runs without `--dry-run`                  | KILLED (3 red)       |
| the clean phase loses `--force`                       | KILLED (18 red)      |
| the dry run never says it asks first                  | KILLED (1 red)       |
| clean reads an n as nobody-to-ask (dies)              | KILLED (1 red)       |
| fullcycle asks BEFORE the preview                     | SURVIVED, now KILLED |
| a failed preview returns 0, so the cycle runs unasked | SURVIVED, now KILLED |
| `ask_person` takes only a lower-case y                | SURVIVED, now KILLED |
| the phase loop back on stdin                          | SURVIVES, declared   |

**The three that survived are now killed** by three arms dc added to `fullcycle.bats` (tagged "0089, dc's review"). Each is green on the unchanged copy and red on its mutant:
- the preview's "--dry-run: nothing was removed" appears before the `[y/N]`;
- a project clean that fails its `--dry-run` stops fullcycle at rc != 0, with no question asked, the clean never run and no build phase;
- a capital `Y` runs the cycle.

The failed-preview mutant was the one that mattered. It turns a failed preview into a cycle that removes the trees without asking. The loop-on-stdin mutant stays declared, as vc's comment in `_fullcycle_run` says: each phase's gate hands its tool `</dev/null`, so no arm can reach it while that holds. With the three arms added, `fullcycle.bats` passes 58 of 58 on the tree.
